page: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v5 is a high-density general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon Platinum 8370C processors, the instance delivers 96 dedicated virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with two threads per core. Hardware-assisted cryptographic and vector instructions are supported, including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA extensions. The instance provides 384.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is CPU-bound with zero GPUs provisioned.

Storage configuration includes 3,865 GB of integrated local solid-state drive capacity alongside Azure Premium Storage capability. Benchmark testing indicates robust data processing capabilities, with PassMark database operations and Redis SET throughput ranking in the upper quartile at over 86 million operations per second. Memory subsystem benchmarks show high throughput, sustaining 324.54 GB/s uncached read bandwidth and 133.41 GB/s uncached write bandwidth. Static web serving throughput reaches 64.48 GB/s.

Multi-core computational throughput is strong across compilation, compression, and rendering benchmarks, including Clang compilation scores of 54,187.0 and Geekbench multi-core scores of 17,654.0. PassMark encryption tests rank within the top ten percent due to hardware VAES and AES acceleration. Conversely, single-thread stress testing and decompression align within median percentiles. Complex generative AI tasks, such as 70-billion-parameter LLM text generation, demonstrate poor execution speeds (2.73 tokens/s) due to the absence of dedicated tensor acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D96ds_v5 maximizes resource consolidation by bundling massive compute, extensive RAM, and significant local SSD storage into a single host slot without GPU overhead. The hardware envelope fits large relational databases, high-capacity Redis caches, static web serving clusters, continuous integration build farms, and multi-threaded ETL pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D96ds_v5 is a high-capacity general-purpose instance featuring 96 dedicated x86_64 virtual CPUs and 48 physical cores powered by 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processors. The instance provides 384.0 GB of memory maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, bundled with 3,865 GB of local SSD storage. It features hardware encryption acceleration, including AES and VAES, driving top-tier cryptographic benchmark results alongside strong multi-core processing in Clang compilation and multi-threaded decompression. Database performance is pronounced, evidenced by Redis throughput exceeding 86 million operations per second and high static web serving bandwidth. Lacking dedicated GPUs, text generation on large language models remains constrained. The instance delivers high resource density for enterprise relational databases, distributed caching layers, web serving platforms, and compute-intensive batch processing workloads.
